source.title: Wide neural networks of any depth evolve as linear models under gradient descent
source.authors: Jaehoon Lee; Lechao Xiao; S. Schoenholz; Yasaman Bahri; Roman Novak; Jascha Narain Sohl-Dickstein; Jeffrey Pennington

record.file_problem: Full paper text supplied, including supplementary material.
record.tranche_reason: Reports training-accuracy curves on CIFAR-10 as part of experiments on linearized training dynamics, but does not state final training-error values in the text.
record.gate_note: CIFAR-10 accuracy curves are shown in figures; the text describes comparisons of training dynamics, not whether classification error reaches zero. Cited convergence results from other papers are not this study's own results.
record.test_reason: Figure 4 reports training accuracy for a randomly initialized convolutional residual network trained with SGD on full CIFAR-10, directly bearing on V1. Its endpoint cannot be recovered from the supplied text.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors prove equivalence to linearized dynamics in the infinite-width limit under stated assumptions and find close finite-width empirical agreement across architectures, optimizers, and losses; they acknowledge settings where agreement deteriorates.
record.recipe_differences: The experiments investigate agreement between network and linearized-model training dynamics; they do not systematically test recipes for reaching zero classification error from random initialization.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports that approximation error varies with width and dataset size (Figure S5), and that cross-entropy logit deviations can grow at late times (Figure S4).

fits_no_version.finding: The MNIST fully connected network and its linearization have similar training dynamics.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Wide fully connected networks trained on MNIST can closely follow their first-order parameter linearizations.

fits_no_version.finding: Linearization agreement improves with width, worsens with dataset size, and can deteriorate for late cross-entropy logits. Figure S5 measures prediction discrepancy between models, not training error against labels.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Sufficiently wide networks can follow approximately linear parameter dynamics under the tested training conditions.

record.problems: The CIFAR-10 accuracy result is only plotted; the text provides no final training-accuracy or training-error value. The paper's main experiments are not designed to test the claim's zero-error outcome.
record.rows_left_out: Figure S2 includes an accuracy plot for binary CIFAR classification, but the caption does not identify a separate training-accuracy value, so it is not extracted as a training-error result. Figure S7 reports final performance across datasets and parameterizations without identifying it as training accuracy.

untested.parts: CIFAR-100, corrupted or random labels, and comparisons involving smaller models, early stopping, or regularized recipes.
Teacher-student ReLU problems, spurious-minimum frequencies, and adding one or two student neurons.
Training-error degradation with depth and controlled comparisons of plain networks against identity-shortcut networks.
Comparative effects of activation-matched initialization, orthogonal versus Gaussian weights, and initialization-dependent trainable depth.

Recovery above the initial stability limit, curvature reduction, edge-of-stability dynamics, and divergence below the threshold. The paper's sufficient small-learning-rate convergence bound does not test these behaviors.
Batch-normalization effects on training speed or learning-rate tolerance, and comparisons against Fixup.

record.verdict_notes: No verdict is justified for V1 without readable training-accuracy values. This measurement limitation is neither evidence against V1 nor a scope limitation. The study is not an original source listed for any version.

versions.untested_parts: Only CIFAR-10 training-accuracy curves are shown, without stated final values. CIFAR-100, corrupted or random labels, smaller models, early stopping, and regularized recipes are not tested.

rows.subject: Wide Residual Network (WRN)
rows.operation_detail: Trained the original network with SGD and momentum on full CIFAR-10 using MSE loss.
rows.note: Training-accuracy curve is plotted; the text gives no final training accuracy or classification-error value.
rows.check: The experiment and version link are appropriate, but the supplied figure text contains no readable curve values establishing final training error. Agreement with the linearized model alone does not establish near-zero error.

rows.subject: ReLU fully connected network
rows.operation_detail: Trained the original network with SGD and momentum on MNIST using cross-entropy loss.
rows.note: MNIST is outside the CIFAR datasets named by V1; the plotted accuracy is included as a related training result, not mapped to V1.
rows.check: V1 names convolutional networks on CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100; this experiment uses a fully connected network on MNIST. Its final training accuracy also cannot be read from the supplied text.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
